subject: strategy
text: | Structured Logs | Every boundary call, state transition, refusal, fault/heal and process lifecycle (the `mcp` role writes no self `process-exit`, Section 7), as the closed `event` enum (Section 3) | **The primary signal.** tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 JSON-per-line, one file per process role under `<home>/diagnostics/`, merged with `events.ndjson` by `agent-run logs` |

subject: strategy
text: | Errors | Panics (a one-line `event:"panic"` record), typed thiserror 2.0.20 errors with fixed `Display`, exit codes plus distinct `detail` codes on `process-exit` (the `mcp` role writes no self `process-exit`, Section 7) | No external reporter: security says "no outbound network calls". A hand-written `std::panic::set_hook`, plus `std::panic::catch_unwind` at the main-thread catch site of every role, around `hook` dispatch, in the `run` PTY pump and handle-wait threads, and around the vt100 feed (Section 7) |

subject: strategy
text: | Metrics | `duration_ms` samples, counts of `event`/`detail` values, `skipped` counts | No in-process instruments and no exporter. Metrics are derived by `jq` over the ndjson; the perf gates run on hyperfine 1.20.0 `--export-json` (Section 5) |

subject: strategy
text: - Every panic after init step 4 produces exactly one single-line structured record in its home-level role file: location, thread, role and instance. The bounded exemptions (the pre-init window, `cli` without an instance, `hook` without `VIOLA_NAME`, a failed step-4 role-file open (a `diagnostics/` folder or file its strict-modes check refuses included), the no-obs-init hidden capture arms (`hook <event> --capture` and `hook statusline --capture`), and a refused instance check on either `viola revive` arm (start or `--list`) or on `viola hook statusline`, or a refused `viola list` scan, which opens none either, or a refused instance check on `viola link` / `viola unlink`, made before their role file opens, or a refused instance check on the six frame verbs (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`), a refused or absent instance on `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths (a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory included), or a refused home tree on `viola run`, `viola revive`'s start or `viola verify`, each made before its role file opens) are listed in Section 10. The payload (one escaped JSON string) and the backtrace (a one-line JSON array of frames) are written only to the instance-scoped detail file (Section 7).

text: | logging-sensitive Vector 4 (hook stdin) | §3 Logging stack (hook sink), §4 Scenario 4, §6 `hook-decision` `detail` codes. The "missing `VIOLA_NAME`" item is **overridden**: no file and no line, asserted by absence (D-16, §4 E1). The "strict-modes failure" item writes no line as landed either: `viola hook statusline`'s refused instance check leaves no trace, asserted by absence (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor). The event and dialog paths' refused or absent instance (a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory included) leaves none either: exit 0 at once, no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame, no SessionEnd append. The "server-verify mismatch" item writes one `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN on Linux and Windows (macOS compares no peer pid, the recorded gap) |
